tasks.instruction: Declare the intended reader, the central question, the intended change in understanding, and the factual boundary. Do not invent facts.
Map the argument or story as consequential units. Each unit needs a function and an expected change; no compulsory fiction beat template.
Write complete passages from the outline. Preserve viewpoint and factual provenance; do not insert invented quotations or evidence.
Reorder, cut, or expand units only when the causal chain, reader understanding, or scene consequence improves.
Edit syntax, cadence, diction and repetition without altering assertions, hedges, attribution, quantities, or narrative knowledge.
Review the finished document against the initial intent, provenance and unresolved editorial questions. Approval is human and separate from automated checks.

limitations: REVIEW_COMPLETE only means human checks were recorded for the exact document version
Review identity and the truth of observations are not independently authenticated
